outcome: Renal function (excretory profile, glomerular filtration rate)
cohort: Pregnant spiny mice were divided into groups fed standard or creatine-supplemented chow, and their offspring were subjected to caesarean delivery or intrauterine asphyxia.
finding: Male offspring exposed to birth asphyxia showed reduced nephron numbers, lower glomerular filtration rate, and increased glomerular collagen IV content, all of which were prevented by maternal creatine supplementation during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Intrauterine asphyxia (compared to caesarean delivery) in spiny mice offspring led to long-term renal dysfunction in males.
gest_age: Pups were delivered one day prior to term (37-d gestation).
